title: Canonical attachment blocks for multimodal prompts
description:
Replace the three per-provider `_format_multimodal` overrides with one canonical attachment block that every provider renders from.

### New module — `src/bespokelabs/curator/types/attachment.py`
- `AttachmentBlock(BaseModel)` with `model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)` — the provider-independent description of one attachment. It carries at least:
  - `kind: t.Literal["image", "document"]`
  - `source: t.Literal["url", "base64"]`
  - `mime_type: str` — always lowercase, no `;`-parameters
  - `payload: str` — the URL when `source == "url"`, else the base64 text
  - `filename: str` — never empty
  - `detail: str | None = None` — a `str` when `kind == "image"`, `None` when `kind == "document"`
- `AttachmentError(ValueError)` — the base class every attachment rejection inherits from.
- `UnknownAttachmentMimeType(AttachmentError)` with `__init__(self, url: str, attachment_type: str)`, storing `self.url` and `self.attachment_type` (the `BaseType.type` ClassVar, i.e. `"image"` or `"file"` — not the block `kind`), message `f"Cannot determine MIME type for {attachment_type} attachment: {url!r}"`.
- `MissingLocalAttachment(AttachmentError)` with `__init__(self, url: str)`, storing `self.url`, message `f"Attachment path is neither an http(s) URL nor an existing file: {url!r}"`.
- `normalize_mime_type(value: str | None) -> str | None` — lowercase, strip surrounding whitespace, drop everything from the first `;`; `None`/`""` map to `None`.
- `_FALLBACK_ATTACHMENT_FILENAME: str = "attachment.bin"`.

### `src/bespokelabs/curator/types/prompt.py`
- Add `BaseType.is_remote` as a property: true iff `url` starts with `http://` or `https://`, case-insensitive.
- Add `_MultiModalPrompt.attachments(self) -> list[BaseType]` returning `self.images + self.files`, in that order, as a new list, leaving the inputs untouched.
- One MIME policy shared by `Image.model_post_init` (line 87) and `File.set_mime_type` (line 103): every MIME value, supplied or guessed, goes through `normalize_mime_type`.
  - When no MIME was supplied and a `url` is present, guess with query and fragment removed: `mimetypes.guess_type(url.split("?", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0])`, so `"https://cdn.example.com/photos/cat.jpeg?size=large"` resolves to `"image/jpeg"`.
  - If the guess fails, `mime_type` stays `None` on both classes and exactly one `logger.warning` is emitted. `Image` no longer falls back to `"image/png"` for a URL.
  - The one surviving default: an `Image` with inline `content`, no `url` and no supplied MIME gets `"image/png"` (matching `_pil_image_to_bytes`, which always saves PNG).
  - Worked values: `File(url="/tmp/x/report.PDF", mime_type="Application/PDF; charset=binary").mime_type == "application/pdf"`; `Image(url="https://example.com/asset").mime_type is None`; `Image(content=b"\x89PNG\r\n").mime_type == "image/png"`.

### `base_online_request_processor.py`
- `BaseOnlineRequestProcessor._canonical_attachment_block(self, data: BaseType) -> AttachmentBlock` converts any `Image` or `File` into a frozen block:
  - `kind` is `"image"` when the resolved `mime_type` starts with the literal `"image/"`, `"document"` otherwise. The Python class is not consulted: `File(url=".../diagram.png")` yields `kind == "image"`, and `Image(content=b"...", mime_type="application/pdf")` yields `kind == "document"`.
  - `detail` is set from the attachment's `detail` attribute for an image block — `"auto"` when the attachment has no such attribute — and is `None` for a document block.
  - `filename` is derived from `os.path.basename(data.url.split("?", 1)[0])` when that is non-empty, else `_FALLBACK_ATTACHMENT_FILENAME`.
  - A remote `url` (per `is_remote`) gives `source == "url"` with the URL as `payload`; anything else gives `source == "base64"` with `BaseType.serialize()` output as `payload`.
  - A non-empty `url` that is not remote must exist as a file (`BaseType.is_local`); when it does not, raise `MissingLocalAttachment(data.url)` — and raise it *before* the MIME check, so `File(url="/tmp/definitely-missing/notes")` (missing and unguessable) raises `MissingLocalAttachment`, not `UnknownAttachmentMimeType`. `File(url="s3://bucket/report.pdf")` also raises `MissingLocalAttachment`. An attachment with inline `content` and no `url` is not subject to this check.
  - When the resolved `mime_type` is `None`, raise `UnknownAttachmentMimeType(url=data.url, attachment_type=data.type)`. This happens at block-build time only: `Image(url=...)` / `File(url=...)` construction itself never raises for a missing MIME.
  - The base still offers every base64 payload to the provider hook, `self.file_upload_limit_check(payload)`, as the current `_format_multimodal` does.
- `def _render_openai_block(block: AttachmentBlock) -> dict` — module level, pure, returning exactly one of:
  - image / url → `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": block.payload, "detail": block.detail}}`
  - image / base64 → `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:{block.mime_type};base64,{block.payload}", "detail": block.detail}}`
  - document / url → `{"type": "file", "file": {"filename": block.filename, "file_url": block.payload}}`
  - document / base64 → `{"type": "file", "file": {"filename": block.filename, "file_data": f"data:{block.mime_type};base64,{block.payload}"}}`
  - No other keys. `detail` is carried on image blocks in the URL case as well as the base64 case.
- `BaseOnlineRequestProcessor._render_attachment_block(self, block: AttachmentBlock) -> dict` returns `_render_openai_block(block)`. This method is the only provider seam; providers see `AttachmentBlock` and nothing else.
- `_format_multimodal(self, data, mime_type=None) -> dict` stays as a back-compatible one-shot: `return self._render_attachment_block(self._canonical_attachment_block(data))`. The `mime_type` argument is ignored.
- `_handle_multi_modal_prompt(self, message: _MultiModalPrompt) -> list[dict]` returns the rendered attachment blocks first — images in list order, then files in list order, exactly `attachments()` — followed by one `{"type": "text", "text": <str>}` per entry of `texts`, in list order. Result length is `len(images) + len(files) + len(texts)`; a new list each call. For `_MultiModalPrompt(texts=["a", "b"], images=[img], files=[doc])` the block types are `["image_url", "file", "text", "text"]`.

### `anthropic_online_request_processor.py`
- Delete the `_format_multimodal` override (lines 111-128).
- Add module-level pure `def _render_anthropic_block(block: AttachmentBlock) -> dict`:
  - url → `{"type": block.kind, "source": {"type": "url", "url": block.payload}}`
  - base64 → `{"type": block.kind, "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": block.mime_type, "data": block.payload}}`
  - No other keys; `detail` and `filename` do not appear. `kind` passes through, so a PDF renders as a `document` block rather than an `image` one.
- `AnthropicOnlineRequestProcessor._render_attachment_block` returns `_render_anthropic_block(block)`.

### `litellm_online_request_processor.py`
- Delete the `_format_multimodal` override (lines 163-181).
- `LiteLLMOnlineRequestProcessor._render_attachment_block` returns `_render_anthropic_block(block)` when `self._uses_anthropic_multimodal_format()` (unchanged, reused as the dispatch key) and `_render_openai_block(block)` otherwise.

### `openai_request_mixin.py` — `calculate_input_tokens` (lines 9-24)
- Today the function does `msg = msg["image_url"]` for every non-`text` block, so an anthropic-shaped block (`{"type": "image", "source": ...}`) or any document block raises `KeyError: 'image_url'`. Rewrite it to dispatch on `block["type"]` using `.get`, never on the absence of a `"text"` key.
- `"text"` costs `len(token_encoding.encode(str(block.get("text", "")), disallowed_special=()))`.
- `"image_url"` and `"image"` both cost `_OPENAI_TOKENS_PER_IMAGE["low"]` (unchanged, 85).
- Add `_OPENAI_TOKENS_PER_DOCUMENT = 1400`; `"file"` and `"document"` blocks both cost it.
- Any other `"type"` costs `0` and raises nothing. A `str` message keeps its current behaviour. The return is an `int`.

### Constraints
- Python `^3.10`; pydantic `>=2.9.2`; no new dependency. Nothing here imports `aiohttp`, opens a socket, sleeps, or spawns anything.
- Reuse as they are: `BaseType.serialize()` (`prompt.py:60`, `prompt.py:110`), `BaseType._is_local_uri` / `_load_file_as_b64` / `is_local` (`prompt.py:21-34`), `_MultiModalPrompt.load` / `.model_validate`, `_unpack_multimodal` (`base_online_request_processor.py:110`), and `_uses_anthropic_multimodal_format` (`litellm_online_request_processor.py:159`).
- Both renderers are module-level pure functions taking only an `AttachmentBlock`, so they can be exercised without constructing a configured processor. Tests build processors with `object.__new__(StubOnline)` — no `config`, no cost processor, no I/O.
- Out of scope: the batch path (`openai_batch_request_processor.py:66`), `File` having no `detail` attribute, and the `self.config.model.split("/")[0]` gate at `litellm_online_request_processor.py:139`.

requirement.rule: The base owns four refusals that no provider can waive, all defined in `attachment.py`. (a) Per-kind byte ceiling: every base64 payload is measured exactly once with `bespokelabs.curator.file_utilities.get_base64_size(payload)` and compared against `_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_LIMIT_MB: dict[str, float] = {"image": 20.0, "document": 24.0}`; strictly greater is a refusal. The measured value is kept on the block as an additional field `size_mb: float | None = None`. (b) Whole-prompt aggregate: `_ATTACHMENT_PROMPT_LIMIT_MB: float = 45.0`; the sum of `size_mb` over the base64 blocks of one `_MultiModalPrompt`, strictly greater than 45.0, is a refusal, and the sum is taken once after every block in the prompt has been built. (c) Count cap: `_ATTACHMENT_COUNT_LIMIT: int = 12`; `len(message.attachments())` strictly greater than 12 is a refusal, evaluated before a single block is built. (d) Empty payload: a `source == "base64"` attachment whose `serialize()` returns `""` is a refusal.
requirement.scope: The per-kind ceiling and the empty-payload check live in `_canonical_attachment_block`; the count cap and the 45.0 MB aggregate live in `_handle_multi_modal_prompt` alone, so `_canonical_attachment_block` and `_format_multimodal` never apply either. The order inside `_canonical_attachment_block` is exactly: `MissingLocalAttachment`; `UnknownAttachmentMimeType`; derive kind/detail/filename and return here for a remote attachment; `payload = data.serialize()` then the empty-payload refusal; then the per-kind ceiling; then `self.file_upload_limit_check(payload)`; then the frozen block. The base ceiling therefore runs before the provider hook, which only ever sees payloads the base already accepted.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: A `source == "url"` block is never measured or read: its `size_mb` is `None`, it contributes nothing to the 45.0 MB sum, and it can never be empty. `texts` are not counted against the 12-attachment cap. Documents are held to 24.0 MB rather than 20.0 MB, so one and the same 24.0 MB base64 payload is refused when `kind == "image"` and accepted (reaching the provider hook) when `kind == "document"`.
requirement.failure_behavior: `AttachmentTooLarge(AttachmentError)` with `__init__(self, kind: str, size_mb: float, limit_mb: float)` storing `.kind`, `.size_mb`, `.limit_mb`, message `f"{kind} attachment is {size_mb} MB, over the {limit_mb} MB limit."` — `kind` is the block kind for the per-attachment ceiling and the literal `"prompt"` for the aggregate. `TooManyAttachments(AttachmentError)` with `__init__(self, count: int, limit: int)` storing `.count`, `.limit`, message `f"Prompt has {count} attachments, over the limit of {limit}."`. `EmptyAttachment(AttachmentError)` with `__init__(self, url: str, filename: str)` storing `.url`, `.filename`, message `f"Attachment {filename} has an empty payload: {url!r}"`. All are `AttachmentError` and therefore `ValueError` subclasses.
requirement.observability: With a stub whose `file_upload_limit_check` appends its argument to `stub.calls`: four images of 18.0/18.0/18.0/6.0 MB base64 (each individually under 20.0) raise `AttachmentTooLarge` with `.kind == "prompt"`, `.size_mb == 60.0`, `.limit_mb == 45.0` and `len(stub.calls) == 4` — the whole prompt was built before the refusal, not abandoned when the running total crossed 45.0 at the third image; the first two of those images alone give a 2-block content list with `len(stub.calls) == 2`. Thirteen copies of `Image(content=b"x")` raise `TooManyAttachments` with `.count == 13`, `.limit == 12` and `stub.calls == []`; twelve give a 12-block list with `len(stub.calls) == 12`; `_MultiModalPrompt(texts=["a"] * 40, images=[tiny])` returns 41 blocks and raises nothing. With a stub whose hook raises `RuntimeError`, `Image(content="A" * 33_554_432)` raises `AttachmentTooLarge(.kind == "image", .size_mb == 24.0, .limit_mb == 20.0)` while the same payload with `mime_type="application/pdf"` raises `RuntimeError`. A zero-byte `tmp/empty.pdf` raises `EmptyAttachment` with `.filename == "empty.pdf"` and `stub.calls == []`, while a zero-byte extension-less `tmp/scratch` raises `UnknownAttachmentMimeType` instead.

fragmentation_sources: chat thread arguing 20 vs 24 MB and where the ceiling belongs relative to file_upload_limit_check
wiki page listing the attachment error taxonomy and the refusal order
mail thread on the 45 MB prompt aggregate and the 12-attachment cap
hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: The aggregate was first checked incrementally, raising as soon as the running total crossed 45.0 MB so trailing attachments were never serialized; it was reversed to a single post-build sum so the reported size_mb is the whole prompt's total.

requirement.rule: `attachment.py` also owns three derived values that `_canonical_attachment_block` computes rather than copies. (a) `_ATTACHMENT_FINGERPRINT_HEX_LEN: int = 12` and a pure `attachment_fingerprint(payload: str) -> str` returning `"sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]`; `AttachmentBlock` gains a required field `fingerprint: str`, set from the block's payload for both sources. (b) `_MAX_ATTACHMENT_FILENAME_LEN: int = 64`: a derived filename longer than 64 characters becomes `name[: 64 - len(ext)] + ext` where `ext = os.path.splitext(name)[1]`, so the result is exactly 64 characters and keeps its extension; when `len(ext) >= 64` the name is simply cut to its first 64 characters; 64 or fewer is untouched. (c) `_SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS: tuple[str, ...] = ("auto", "low", "high")` and a pure `normalize_detail(value: str | None) -> str` returning `str(value).strip().lower()` when that lands in `_SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS` and `"auto"` otherwise; an image block's `detail` is `normalize_detail(getattr(data, "detail", "auto"))`.
requirement.scope: All three happen at block-build time, inside `_canonical_attachment_block`, and touch only the `AttachmentBlock`: `Image.detail` keeps whatever raw string the caller wrote, `data.url` is never rewritten, and `block.payload` keeps the full untruncated URL or base64 text. The fingerprint of a `source == "url"` block is taken over the URL string exactly as given, query and fragment included; the digest is always over the payload *string*, never over decoded bytes, and never over the other block fields.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: None of this metadata reaches a provider: `_render_openai_block` and `_render_anthropic_block` still compare `==` to the dicts the ticket tabulates, so no `"fingerprint"` and no `"size_mb"` key appears in an `image_url`, `file`, `image` or `document` block — what the OpenAI `file` block carries is the capped `filename` beside the full untruncated `file_url`, and what its `image_url` block carries is the normalized `detail`. A document block keeps `detail is None` and is never given a normalized detail.
requirement.failure_behavior: An unsupported detail string is downgraded, not rejected and not passed through: `Image(content=b"x", detail="ultra")` builds a block with `detail == "auto"` and emits exactly one `logger.warning`; a supported value emits none, and `normalize_detail(None) == "auto"` with no warning. Constructing the `Image` itself never raises for an unknown detail.
requirement.observability: `attachment_fingerprint("JVBERi0xLjQK") == "sha256:fc1c4358d4aa"`; for `tmp/report.pdf` holding `b"%PDF-1.4\n"`, `stub._canonical_attachment_block(File(url=str(tmp / "report.pdf"))).fingerprint == "sha256:fc1c4358d4aa"`; `Image(url="https://cdn.example.com/photos/cat.jpeg?size=large")` gives `.fingerprint == "sha256:80ce7facd006"` and `Image(content=b"x")` gives `"sha256:5e21d86b709b"`. `File(url="https://cdn.example.com/reports/2024-q4-consolidated-financial-statements-and-notes-final-approved-v3.pdf")` renders as `{"type": "file", "file": {"filename": "2024-q4-consolidated-financial-statements-and-notes-final-ap.pdf", "file_url": <the full 73-character-basename URL>}}`; a basename of exactly 64 characters passes through unchanged; a 72-character extension-less basename yields `"ledger-entries-consolidated-2024-q4-final-copy-for-review-board-"`. `b(Image(content=b"x", detail="HIGH")).detail == "high"`, `b(Image(content=b"x", detail=" Low ")).detail == "low"`, `b(Image(content=b"x", detail="ultra")).detail == "auto"`, and `_render_openai_block(b(Image(content=b"x", detail="HIGH")))` equals `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,eA==", "detail": "high"}}`.

fragmentation_sources: chat thread about de-duplicating attachments in logs and caches, settling on a short sha256 prefix over the payload string
wiki note on provider filename length complaints
mail thread on a caller shipping detail='HIGH' and the decision to downgrade rather than reject
hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: The fingerprint was first taken over the decoded bytes with url blocks left unfingerprinted; it was reversed to hashing the payload string so a url block has an id too.

brief:
Multimodal attachments: what block an image or a non-image file becomes on the way
to a provider, who is allowed to reject one for being too big, and what one costs.

The area, concretely:
- `src/bespokelabs/curator/types/prompt.py` — two MIME policies, twenty lines apart.
  `Image.model_post_init` (line 87) ends `self.mime_type = mime_type.lower() if
  mime_type else "image/png"`: an unguessable type becomes a default, and warns.
  `File.set_mime_type` (line 103) ends `return mime_type.lower() if mime_type else
  None`: the same situation yields nothing, and says nothing.
- `src/bespokelabs/curator/request_processor/online/base_online_request_processor.py`
  — `_format_multimodal` (line 134) emits `{"type": "image_url", ...}` for `Image`
  and `File` alike, having first done `mime_type = mime_type or "image/png"`
  (line 136), so a `File` whose MIME could not be guessed is formatted as a PNG.
  `_handle_multi_modal_prompt` (line 159) feeds both lists through it.
- The provider subclasses disagree about the block vocabulary:
  `anthropic_online_request_processor.py` (lines 111-128) always emits
  `{"type": "image", ...}` with `media_type` and never a document block;
  `litellm_online_request_processor.py` (line 169) picks `"image" if "image" in
  mime_type else "document"`; the openai path inherits the base. Remote URLs take a
  different shape again in each.
- Three size checks that between them cover very little: anthropic's (lines 199-205,
  against `_ANTHROPIC_ALLOWED_IMAGE_SIZE_MB = 20`), openai's (lines 250-254), and
  litellm's (lines 138-145), which is gated on `self.config.model.split("/")[0]`
  against a `{"openai": 20}` table — so `"openai/gpt-4o"` is checked and `"gpt-4o"`
  is not. All three are reached only from the base64 branch, so a remote URL is never
  checked by any of them. The size itself is approximated from the base64 length in
  `file_utilities.py` (lines 25-29).
- `src/bespokelabs/curator/request_processor/openai_request_mixin.py` —
  `calculate_input_tokens` (lines 9-24) assumes every non-text block is
  `msg["image_url"]` and charges a flat 85 tokens, so an anthropic-shaped or
  `document` block raises `KeyError`. Anthropic charges a flat 1024; litellm declares
  1024 for an image and 2048 for a document.
- `openai_batch_request_processor.py:66` declares multimodal support, but the
  unpacking (`_unpack_multimodal`) exists only on the online base and is called only
  from there, so the batch path serializes the raw prompt object.

Nothing states whether there is one canonical block vocabulary that providers
translate out of or whether each provider owns its own shape; what an unguessable
MIME type should do, and whether images and non-images answer that the same way;
whether a size ceiling is per provider, per kind or global, and whether it applies to
a remote URL; or what a non-image attachment costs an estimator. Read all of it and
design one attachment-to-payload policy.

Out of scope: do not build the specification around the two one-line defects a
careful reader fixes unaided — that `File` has no `detail` attribute, and that
`split("/")[0]` misses an unprefixed model name. Grade the policy, not the typos.

Constraints: pure and deterministic, no network, no sleeping, no threads. Testable by
constructing `Image`, `File` and `_MultiModalPrompt` directly, and by driving a
concrete stub subclass of `BaseOnlineRequestProcessor` — `file_upload_limit_check` is
abstract, so the stub must supply it. A temp-directory file for the local branch and a
fake encoder object with `.encode()` are the only fixtures allowed. The suite must not
depend on `tests/integrations/test_multimodal.py`'s VCR cassettes or output hashes.
